case.title: The Missing Traveler
case.description: Matej vanished in these parts, leaving behind his horse and several paid nights. The record of his departure looks far too convenient.
objective.search.name: Find the missing traveler's trail
objective.search.active: The trail leads into the marked area. Somewhere here lies the truth of Matej's disappearance.
objective.investigation.name: Uncover Matej's fate
objective.target.name: Hunt down Matej's killer
objective.target.active: The evidence is conclusive. Find the guilty man and carry out the sentence.
objective.target.done: Matej's killer is dead. Now no trace can be left behind.
objective.cleanup.name: Leave no trace
objective.cleanup.active: The killing is done. Make certain no one can connect it to Henry.
objective.cleanup.witnessed: Someone saw too much. Witnesses may lead the guards to the truth.
objective.cleanup.clean: No alarm was raised. The case can be closed.
objective.cleanup.controlled: Every dangerous witness is gone. The case can be closed.
objective.cleanup.noisy: The alarm was raised, but the pursuit lost the trail. The case is closed, though not without consequence.
objective.cleanup.external: The guilty man died without Henry's hand. No trail remains.
objective.guidance.listen.name: Listen to the conversations in the inn yard
objective.guidance.listen.active: The inn yard is crowded. Someone may let slip what happened to Matej.
direction.paper: Question the local innkeeper or search for the records yourself.
direction.witness: Find an inn worker and ask about Matej's horse.
direction.overheard: Listen to the conversations around the inn.
direction.ledger: The innkeeper hid the guest ledger in one of the upstairs chests. Someone else wrote Matej's departure line, so the book is worth examining.
dialogue.rumor.henryMissing: I hear one of your guests disappeared.
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperLeft: He did not disappear. He left before dawn. At least, that is what the guest ledger says.
dialogue.rumor.henryHorse: Then why leave his horse behind?
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperHorse: That is what troubles me. He paid three nights ahead, then vanished. By morning his horse was back in the stable, already unsaddled.
dialogue.rumor.henryName: What was his name? What brought him here?
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperMatej: Matej. A petty merchant. He was carrying money to a companion's widow — the man died on the road, and Matej swore his family would receive their share.
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperHand: Not me. The line appeared that morning, in a hand I did not know. I locked the book away after that.
dialogue.rumor.innkeeperChest: It is upstairs. I hid it in one of the chests. I will not give you a key. If someone wrote a lie in my book, I would rather not know how you reached it.
dialogue.rumor.foundHenryHand: You did not write the line saying Matej left.
dialogue.rumor.foundInnkeeperChest: So you got to the ledger after all. You could not have had a key.
dialogue.rumor.foundHenryNote: The hand is different. And the note between the pages says someone lured him past the old willow.
dialogue.rumor.foundInnkeeperHorse: Then he did not leave of his own accord. His horse came back without him and was in the stable before dawn.
dialogue.rumor.foundInnkeeperBoguslav: I do not know. One of the inn workers was with the horses that night. If he saw anything, he will not speak of it willingly.
dialogue.witness.prompt: Ask an inn worker about Matej's horse
dialogue.witness.henryHorse: You tend the horses. Do you remember the merchant Matej's mount?
dialogue.witness.bretislavRemembers: A bay, white fetlock on the hind leg. Matej rode out in the night. Before dawn, the horse was back in its stall.
dialogue.witness.bretislavReturned: A local man led it in. Mud on his boots, something dark on his sleeve. He said Matej had continued on foot.
dialogue.witness.bretislavSaw: Clearly enough. He pressed a coin into my hand and told me to forget who held the reins.
dialogue.witness.bretislavWarning: The next day a dead crow lay on my threshold. I understood. Not every truth is worth one's neck.
dialogue.witness.bretislavFire: Later he burned something by the old willow. It smelled of scorched wool. In the morning I found a blackened clasp from a travelling cloak.
dialogue.witness.henryPoint: You will point this man out to me.
dialogue.witness.bretislavPoint: I will. But after that, you and I never spoke.
objective.witness.name: Question a witness from the inn
objective.witness.active: According to the innkeeper, one of the inn workers may have seen who returned Matej's horse without its rider.
objective.witness.done: The witness saw a local man return Matej's horse alone, then burn something by the road. He identified the suspect.
objective.witness.fallbackDone: The witness saw a local man return Matej's horse alone and destroy evidence by the road. He identified the suspect.
action.listen.progress: You listen to what people are saying…
action.listen.unavailable: It is too quiet here now.
document.ledger.name: Torn Guest-Ledger Page
document.ledger.info: A page from the local inn ledger. The departure line is in another hand, and a note was hidden between the leaves.
document.ledger.body:
Matej of Ledetchko. Three nights paid.

Left before matins.

The last line is written in darker ink and another hand. A folded scrap lies between the pages:

If I do not return, the money in my purse belongs to Marketa, Pavel's widow. A local man learned of it and spent the evening asking how much I carried and who expected me. At dawn he means to show me a shorter road past the old willow.

He is too obliging for a man who wants nothing from me. But if I am wrong, I shall be far away by noon.

Matej
journal.rumor: Matej's horse returned without its rider. Someone at the inn noticed that the record of his departure was written in another hand, and the torn page was hidden in one of the chests. I should find and read it.
journal.rumorAfterLedger: They confirmed it at the inn: the same farmhand who returned Matej's horse tore out the page. I should find the witness by the stables or listen to the talk in the yard.
journal.ledger: The record of Matej's departure was written by another hand. He hid a note between the pages: someone learned about the money for Marketa the widow and offered him a shorter road past the old willow. The horse returned alone. I should learn who was near the horses that night.
journal.witness: A witness by the stables identified the man who returned Matej's horse before dawn. He was nervous and in a hurry to leave. Now I have someone worth following.
journal.overheard: People in the inn yard remembered an argument before Matej vanished: it concerned Marketa's money and the short road past the old willow. Someone knew both the sum and the route too well. I should look into the man connected to Matej's horse.
trophy.description: A red feather taken from the killer's body. A silent reminder that Matej's debt was finally collected.
